data_requests.item: Existing boiler blowdown service, treatment/control and recovery basis (qualified records first)
where: site records: Named boiler operating and water-treatment records: distinguish bottom/mud removal of suspended solids from surface/skimming removal of dissolved solids; retain asset/source/revision, sample time, availability, quantity/units and operating coverage. Review existing suitable control and recovery before requesting more data.

a walkdown: Only if the relevant records cannot settle an applicable boiler-water question: agree with the responsible engineer what safe observation or measurement is still needed; no blanket new field measurement or hardware instruction.
data_requests.how: First establish the actual steam/water service and bottom versus surface function. Normally manual intermittent bottom blowdown alone is not an automation fault. An analyzer tag or nearby location does not prove boiler-water association, suitable control or adequate operation. Keep TDS and conductivity units, representative sampling and feedwater/makeup/condensate distinctions explicit. Any calculated blowdown fraction or percent must state its justified balance, denominator and time basis; do not impose the source's contextual range as a target. For applicable continuous surface duty, review pressure, actual rate/hours, installed recovery, receiving duty and constraints before considering an investigation. Known dry/non-water service is not applicable; unknown service needs clarification. Complete suitable records can be acknowledged without a new measurement or retrofit. Proportional makeup-water-flow control can be an existing surface-control arrangement; absence of a conductivity probe alone is not a control defect. Keep steam-flow and feedwater-flow rate denominators distinct; neither a source screening sentence nor its worked table supplies a universal target.

questions.decision_rule: Review records and unresolved applicability with the responsible engineer. Distinguish bottom/mud and surface/skimming functions; manual practice or a missing/generic analyzer does not authorize automation. Consider further control or heat-recovery investigation only if applicable service, treatment needs, actual operation and recovery/sink constraints establish a remaining question. No hardware decision, operating change, chemistry target or site saving follows from this screen.

typical_benefit.wording: "Blowdown rates typically range from 4% to 8% of boiler feedwater flow rate, but can be as high as 10%." LBNL (as reported in LBNL-56183): blowdown heat recovery 1.3%, 1-2.7 yr.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.124x (IAC/ITAC browse page: 334 recommendations, 1.6 yr average payback, 36.7% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)

questions.limits: Source-informed records review: DOE Steam Tip 9, pp. 1–2, distinguishes bottom and surface functions and includes proportional makeup-water-flow control. Supplemental Tip 10, pp. 1–2 (https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2014/05/f16/steam10_boiler_blowdown.pdf), qualifies recovery by actual source and receiving duty; its opening steam-rate screen and feedwater-based example have different denominators. Historical S19/S24/IAC benefit figures are inherited, not reverified, site-specific or current-standard acceptance. Supplied candidate fields do not establish engineering adequacy or source authority.
